data.reason:
I am deciding for the regulation officer. I keep constitution-v1 (vote.quorum 2), which follows the LLM's recommendation.

The customer case for proposal 1 has weakened:
- On-time rises 213.6 → 219.4 (+5.8), but the improvement held on only 3/5 seeds, against 5/5 earlier.
- Its extra gain over proposal 2, which passes by vote and was adopted in D3, is about 3.6 on-time deliveries (219.4 vs 215.8).

Its costs are larger:
- Road violations rise 24.2 → 34.8.
- C, already the lowest, falls 58.3 → 46.9.
- B falls 69.6 → 62.5.
- sanction_total, which the operator required in K1 before any referral, is still not measured.

Lowering the quorum to 1 is a lasting change. From then on, any single company could push through rules that pass check, the constitution and the improvement test. B and C, and indirectly customers, would lose the protection of broad support on every future rule. I will not trade that lasting governance safeguard for one uncertain gain. The votes (A ○, B ×, C ×) still stand.

A proposal 1 variant, or a compensated version, can come back once sanction_total is reported and the gain is re-confirmed across seeds. That path needs no change to the regulation.
assumptions: Proposal 2 (hold_limit 50s), adopted in D3, stays in force and keeps its measured gains.
Future votes under quorum 2 can still adopt rules that benefit customers if they are compensated or designed differently.
The 3/5 seeds result reflects a real weakening of proposal 1's gain, or noise. It is not hiding a larger gain.
unknowns: sanction_total under proposal 1 and under proposal 2.
Why B and C reject block_k 3 → 2, and whether a compensation would make it votable.
The combined effect of block_k 3 → 2 on top of hold_limit 50s.
How companies would use quorum 1 on future rules.
